question: persister
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out using patient-derived samples. Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Lineage-barcoded patient-derived organoids with twin splitting
ideas.description: Barcode a patient-derived organoid or PDX line at high complexity, split it into an untreated reference arm and a drug-treated arm, and test whether the surviving barcodes are reproducibly the same across replicate splits. Reproducible survivors indicate a heritable pre-existing state, while random survivors indicate stochastic induction, and the untreated twin allows direct profiling of survivor ancestors before drug exposure.

ideas.title: Serial pre-treatment, on-treatment, and progression biopsies at single-cell resolution
ideas.description: Collect matched biopsies from the same patients at baseline, at the residual-disease nadir 2-4 weeks into targeted therapy, and at relapse, and profile all three by single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. The residual-disease timepoint is the only direct window onto persister cells in a human tumor and reveals whether the persister program pre-exists in a rare subpopulation or appears only under drug.

ideas.title: Spatially resolved mapping of residual disease in on-treatment biopsies
ideas.description: Use imaging-based spatial transcriptomics or multiplexed protein imaging on on-treatment patient biopsies to determine whether surviving cells occupy non-random positions such as perivascular, hypoxic, invasive-front, or CAF- and immune-shielded niches. This separates cell-intrinsic tolerance programs from microenvironment-provided protection, which have very different therapeutic consequences.

ideas.title: Whole-genome and clonal phylogeny analysis of survivor populations
ideas.description: Perform deep whole-genome sequencing and single-cell copy-number profiling on matched pre-treatment and residual or relapse patient samples to test whether survivors carry pre-existing resistance mutations, subclonal expansions, or no genetic distinction at all. Reconstructing the clonal phylogeny establishes whether relapse derives from a genetically privileged clone or from genetically identical cells in a permissive transcriptional state.

ideas.title: Live ex vivo drug exposure of fresh malignant effusions and circulating tumor cells
ideas.description: Expose freshly isolated pleural effusion, ascites, or CTC-derived tumor cells from patients to the targeted agent under live-cell imaging, then sort survivors for matched single-cell transcriptomic and proteomic analysis. Repeat sampling from the same patient across multiple taps tests whether the tolerant state is stable and heritable or transient and reversible.
